sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Clicking on the handle also only changed the HUD (the bar shrank by 2 cells: (63,61),(63,62) G→c). In other words, the bottom bar shrinks by 1 cell per action (step). This is the step/timer bar.
So, single clicks on the piece do nothing visible. Maybe the interaction is a drag: MOUSE down on the piece, then MOUSE at the destination = drag. But since each MOUSE action is a single click, maybe the game treats consecutive clicks as a drag? Or maybe the game is "click a piece, then click the target" — the first click selected it (no visual), and the second click should move it. But the second click was on the handle of the same piece, so nothing happened.
Let me try the 2-click hypothesis: click the green piece (select), then click the center of the left green slot in the upper-right container (21,39). If the piece moves, the hypothesis is confirmed.
Actually, wait. Maybe the intended mechanic is this: the piece moves toward the clicked cell, one step at a time? The first click was on the piece itself (no movement). Let me try clicking a cell to the right of the green piece, e.g. (10,40), and see if the piece moves right.
Which hypothesis is more likely? In many of these ARC grid click games: click a piece to select it, click the destination to move it. Let me test the selection hypothesis: click the green piece, then click the green slot.
But note: each click consumes 1 step of the HUD bar. The bar is 64 cells; probably 64 steps total. I've used 2 so far. No problem.
Let me batch execute: click the green piece at (10,30), then click the slot at (21,39). Then take the diff.
